subject: SummitTech: Special uptime terms and operational onboarding
messages:
From: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@summittech.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Larkin <maya@summittech.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: written uptime + latency commitment and onboarding runbook

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. SummitTech has a hard requirement for mission-critical traffic: we need a written availability commitment covering our production tenant (single-region, US-East) and a latency guardrail of p95 < 95ms for our normal load profile. The legal and ops teams are asking for two things before we proceed: 1) a short operational runbook that describes on-call escalation and what happens if the commitment is missed; 2) any pricing/credits or contractual language you can provide for an exception to standard terms.

We understand this is non-standard, but this is effectively a gateway for our expansion — if you can document the fallback policies and an onboarding checklist, we can route procurement and legal immediately.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Put SummitTech on a reserved pool or similar so we can hit predictable p95;
- Provide a fallback model (lower-cost variant) and automated routing if capacity spikes;
- Commit to an operational playbook and an agreed credit/penalty structure in the contract?

I've attached our compliance overview for context (see SummitTech-Compliance-Requirements.pdf).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of Platform, SummitTech
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@summittech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: written uptime + latency commitment and onboarding runbook

Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear ask and the compliance doc. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Priyom (Solutions) to map the operative path. High-level: we can support dedicated reserved capacity + a compatible fallback model, but a formalized credit/penalty clause and the exact p95 guarantee require alignment across Product and Cloud Ops.

Marissa / Priyom — can you two own drafting a short operational runbook and a proposed commercial scope (including an example credit table) for SummitTech? Ideally we capture: reserved pool size assumptions, expected cache warmers, fallback model description, monitoring & SLIs, and a one-page escalation playbook.

I’ll coordinate with legal once you have a proposed approach. Rajiv — will you share target SLO language from procurement/legal if you have it?

—Logan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@summittech.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 14:11:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed timeline and pilot for SummitTech uptime terms

Rajiv / Logan —

Thanks — putting a pragmatic plan on the table:
- Week 0–1: Priyom and CS spin up an operational runbook draft and sizing worksheet.
- Week 1–2: We provision a reserved pool (trial commit) and run a 2-week pilot with synthetic and real traffic; monitoring hooks for p95 and request success rate.
- Week 3: Review pilot metrics and translate into contract language + credit table.

Commercial note: for reserved capacity + a written p95 commitment we typically expect a minimum 6-month reserved term; for a first pass I’m proposing a 10% one-time credit if SLAs are missed (example values in Proposed-MAP.xlsx attached).

Attachments: Proposed-MAP.xlsx (pricing examples), Operational-Runbook-Draft.md (skeleton).

Next steps: Priyom — can you confirm whether the warmers and cache priming noted in the runbook are sufficient to meet p95 <95ms for the expected SummitTech traffic shape?

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 09:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed timeline and pilot for SummitTech uptime terms — technical clarifications

Marissa / team —

Quick technical clarifications from the SE side:
1) Warmup / cache strategy: we will need an automated KV cache warmer and prefix caching for SummitTech's top-50 routes; that is supported but requires an initialization job before cutover.
2) Reserved pool sizing: we need to agree on QPS and token/sec targets. For an expected 200 QPS steady (with peaks up to 450), my initial sizing is 6 x A100 equiv nodes in a reserved pool for US-East. This assumes 8k sequence average.
3) Fallback behavior: product supports routing to a quantized model variant (faster, lower-cost) — this preserves availability but will have measurable quality delta. We should document allowable fallback in the runbook and contract.

Questions for Product (Lauren): are we comfortable committing to p95 <95ms with the reserved pool + warmers at the sizing above, and can we offer an automated fallback switch that is auditable in the Console?

—Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 17:50:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed timeline and pilot for SummitTech uptime terms — product constraints and recommended ops path

Team —

Thanks — technical summary and recommended exception path:

Constraints:
- We can’t guarantee p95 <95ms on shared, on-demand pools for large-peak patterns; an SLA requires capacity reservation or a dedicated cluster.
- Quantized fallback model can bring per-token latency down ~20–35% but will change output characteristics; we must include a clear QA/guardrail in the contract.

Recommended path for a written commitment:
1) Dedicated reserved cluster (customer-locked capacity) in US-East for SummitTech for the contract term.
2) Pre-deployment cache priming job and scheduled warmers in the runbook (step-by-step included in Operational-Runbook-Draft.md).
3) Automated fallback policy: when cluster CPU/GPU pressure > 85% for > 3 minutes, route 100% of new sessions to the quantized variant; log and notify on-call.
4) Monitoring & SLI: p95 latency, request success, formal incident SLA windows.
5) Credits: example table is fine as a starting point; legal to finalize wording.

I’ll attach a one-page ops checklist (paste below) you can include in the contract exhibit. Also: we can include a 24/7 on-call escalation contact for the pilot phase (Grace will manage).

--- Ops checklist (one-page) ---
- Reserved cluster size and node types (confirmed by SE)
- Cache priming schedule and owner
- On-call rotation and escalation matrix
- Fallback model behavior and audit logs
- Pilot acceptance criteria (p95, error rate, stability)

Lauren
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Agarwal <rajiv@summittech.ai>, Maya Larkin <maya@summittech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, contracts@summittech.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 20:03:00 +0000
Subject: SummitTech: operational runbook & next steps (pilot + contract exhibit)

Rajiv / Maya —

Thanks for the patience while we scoped this. Attached is a consolidated runbook and the pricing MAP (Proposed-MAP.xlsx) we discussed. Summary of agreed next steps:

1) Pilot provisioning (Week 1): Redwood provisions a dedicated reserved cluster in US-East sized per Priyom's estimate (6 x A100 equiv). We will run cache priming and a two-week pilot.
2) Monitoring & acceptance (Week 1–3): We will instrument p95, success rate, and failover logs. Acceptance: p95 < 95ms for the pilot window and error rate < 0.5%.
3) Fallback & audit: If load crosses the threshold, we will failover to the quantized variant and log the event; we will share the audit logs for the incident.
4) Contract exhibit: Legal teams to review the Exhibit A (ops checklist + credit table). Link to DocuSign for initial term-sheet: https://docusign.com/xyz123-summittech-uptime.

Please confirm: 1) pilot start date (we propose Wed 2026-02-11) and 2) whether the proposed credit table in the MAP is acceptable for legal to start drafting.

Attached: Operational-Runbook-Draft.md, Proposed-MAP.xlsx, SummitTech-Compliance-Requirements.pdf

Thanks — we’ll be on standby to kick off as soon as you confirm.

—Logan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
